source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993)
finding: Preregistered, double-blind replication of the 1993 violin study did not reproduce the core result. Best and good violinists did not differ in accumulated solo practice to age 18.
numbers: Replication: best n=13, good n=13, less accomplished n=13 (Cleveland Institute of Music, Case Western). Practice alone to 18: best M=8224 h; original best 7410, good 5301, teachers 3420. Chi2(2)=13.90, eta2=0.26.
quote: we found no statistically significant differences in accumulated practice alone to age 18 between the best and good violinists
limits: Cleveland sample may be more skilled than the Berlin sample (more competitions). Small n. Retrospective estimates.
agent_relevance: Practice volume did not separate top from good performers; do not assume training time alone explains top skill.

source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993)
finding: Effect size was about half of the original. Original comparison explained 48% of performance variance; replication explained 26%, close to the 23% music meta-analytic mean.
numbers: Original 48% vs replication 26% (eta2=0.26) vs meta-analytic music mean 23%.
limits: Same grouping by faculty nomination and department. Original used a lenient F test; replication used standard analyses.
agent_relevance: Early striking effects shrink under blind, standard analysis; expect shrinkage for any one-study scaffold gain.

source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993)
finding: Teacher-designed practice (the theoretical definition of deliberate practice) was tested for the first time and gave a similar pattern to practice alone.
numbers: Authors found no earlier empirical study that measured teacher-designed practice alone as the definition. Results were similar when restricted to teacher-designed activities.
limits: Self-report; both estimates collected in the same session (teacher-designed asked after practice alone).
agent_relevance: The two definitions of deliberate practice are separable and measurable; definitional drift is a central dispute.

source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993)
finding: At least one of the best violinists must have caught up from less accumulated practice than some good violinists, which contradicts the claim that catching up is impossible.
numbers: Original claim p.393: 'impossible for an individual with less accumulated practice at some age to catch up'. Replication: most best violinists had less solo practice than the good-group mean.
limits: Retrospective recall; accuracy of estimates not independently checked.
agent_relevance: Late catch-up is possible; rate of learning, not only hours, matters.

source: Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald (2014) Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis
finding: Meta-analysis across domains found deliberate practice explains a modest share of performance variance, falling as the domain becomes less regular.
numbers: Variance explained: games 26%, music 21%, sports 18%, education 4%, professions under 1%.
quote: We conclude that deliberate practice is important, but not as important as has been argued.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. Its definition of deliberate practice was broad (structured activities to improve), which Ericsson criticised.
agent_relevance: Stable, rule-bound domains (games, music) reward practice most; messy professional domains much less.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Table of meta-analyses shows the overall practice-performance correlation lies between 0.38 and 0.56 depending on inclusion rule, never near 1.
limits: Table is from authors who are critics of the strong deliberate practice view.
agent_relevance: The r = 0.40 figure in our subfield table matches Miller et al. (2019); treat it as one of several estimates from .38 to .61.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Correcting for unreliability of practice and performance measures raises the correlation, but even at generous reliability the explained variance is below 100% except for music (Platz).
numbers: At reliability .70: Macnamara 2014 corrected r=.54 (29.5%); Platz .87 (75.9%); sports .64 (41.3%); Miller .57 (32.7%); E&H .80 (64.0%). At .60: Platz 1.00. At .90: Macnamara 2014 .42 (17.8%).
limits: Reliability of retrospective practice estimates is assumed (E&H argue about 0.6), not measured in most studies.
agent_relevance: Disagreement is partly psychometric; report both raw and corrected effect sizes.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Hambrick et al. 2014 reanalysis found practice leaves most variance unexplained even after reliability correction.
numbers: Reliable variance explained by deliberate practice: chess 34%, music 29.9%.
quote: This is a substantial amount of variance, but it is not enough to support the claim
limits: Authors are critics; text read in full.
agent_relevance: A large unexplained remainder means other levers (ability, task selection, prior knowledge) matter.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Ericsson and Harwell kept only 14 of 88 studies from the 2014 meta-analysis, and seven of their eight deliberate-practice effect sizes came from studies Ericsson had earlier rejected.
numbers: 14 of 88 studies retained (8 deliberate practice effects, 6 purposeful practice effects). Ericsson 2014 had rejected 87 of the 88.
limits: This is the critics' account of a rival's analysis; the rival disputes it.
agent_relevance: Inclusion criteria drive the answer; any evidence synthesis for the agent should publish its filter.

source: Ericsson & Harwell (2019) Deliberate practice and proposed limits on the effects of practice on the acquisition of expert performance
finding: Rival meta-analysis using a strict definition (solitary or coached practice aimed at specific performance goals) found a large correlation.
numbers: Corrected r=0.61 (36% of variance) overall. Sample-weighted: games r=.50 (k=5), music r=.71 (k=3), sports r=.58 (k=5), education r=.31 (k=1), professions k=0.
limits: Only a small subset of studies passed three criteria; no profession study qualified; education had one (Spelling Bee). Authors are the original theory holders.
agent_relevance: Under strict definitions practice matters more, but the strict set is tiny and mostly games, music, sports.

source: Ericsson & Harwell (2019) Deliberate practice and proposed limits on the effects of practice on the acquisition of expert performance
finding: Authors argue the 2014 and 2016 meta-analyses are too broad (any structured practice) and that restriction of range hides the effect among elites.
numbers: Reliability of retrospective practice estimates about 0.6-0.8 for last 1-2 years; athlete-parent agreement r=.59 (Baker 2003); long-interval estimates not significantly correlated (Ward 2007).
limits: The range-restriction argument is plausible but untested: none of the elite-only studies passed their criteria.
agent_relevance: Measurement quality of the predictor limits any conclusion; for an agent, log actual practice instead of relying on recall.

source: Ericsson & Harwell (2019) Deliberate practice and proposed limits on the effects of practice on the acquisition of expert performance
finding: Dispute about definition: Ericsson and Harwell call the 2014 definition 'structured practice' and say it is not the original deliberate practice.
numbers: Macnamara 2014 included e.g. nurse education lecture hours and bowling team practice; E&H exclude team practice and lectures.
limits: The definition gap explains a large part of the effect-size disagreement.
agent_relevance: Results depend on whether practice has expert-designed goals and feedback, i.e. how the loop is built, not time spent.

source: Ericsson & Harwell (2019) Deliberate practice and proposed limits on the effects of practice on the acquisition of expert performance
finding: Ericsson and Harwell reanalysed Hambrick and Tucker-Drob twin data with music achievement matched to the Berlin academy level, and the additive genetic effect was no longer significant.
numbers: Mosing 2014: over 10,000 twins, heritability of music ability 40-70%. E&H reanalysis of Hambrick & Tucker-Drob 2015 not significant (their Supplementary Text S1).
limits: Reanalysis by the theory holder; few professionals in the samples; E&H say Mosing and Ullen never published an analysis for professionals despite requests.
agent_relevance: Genetics versus practice remains open at the professional level.

source: Macnamara, Moreau & Hambrick (2016) The relationship between deliberate practice and performance in sports: a meta-analysis
finding: Practice explained 18% of sports variance but only about 1% among elite athletes; higher-skill athletes did not start earlier.
numbers: Overall 18% of variance; elite level about 1%.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. E&H argue the elite result reflects range restriction.
agent_relevance: Diminishing returns of practice at the top: the lever may stop working for the best performers.

source: Macnamara & Hambrick (2016) How important is deliberate practice? Reply to Ericsson (2016)
finding: Authors restate that practice accounts for 18% in sport but leaves a much larger share unexplained, and say Ericsson's critique has errors and omissions.
numbers: 18% of sports variance.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session.
agent_relevance: Shows the dispute is about interpretation of the same numbers.

source: Mosing, Madison, Pedersen, Kuja-Halkola, Ullen (2014) Practice does not make perfect: no causal effect of music practice on music ability
finding: Twin study: identical twins who differ in practice do not differ in music ability, so the practice-ability link is mostly genetic.
numbers: N=10,500 Swedish twins. Practice-ability correlations .18 to .36. Heritability of practice 40-70%.
quote: when genetic predisposition was controlled for, more practice was no longer associated with better music skills
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. Outcome is music discrimination ability, not professional success (E&H objection).
agent_relevance: Practice amount can be a marker of aptitude; correlation is not proof of a training effect.

source: Meinz & Hambrick (2010) Deliberate practice is necessary but not sufficient to explain individual differences in piano sight-reading skill
finding: Working memory capacity added to prediction beyond deliberate practice, and practice did not reduce its effect.
numbers: Deliberate practice explained nearly half of sight-reading variance; working memory capacity had a further positive effect.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session.
agent_relevance: Capacity limits are not removed by training; a scaffold cannot replace base capacity.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Fluid intelligence matters more at low skill than at high skill in chess, but age confounds this.
numbers: Burgoyne 2016 meta-analysis: fluid intelligence-chess rating r=0.32 at lower skill, r=0.14 at higher skill. Burgoyne 2019: general intelligence explained about 30% of individual differences in rate of learning a simple piano piece.
limits: Skill level confounded with age (youth in low-skill samples).
agent_relevance: Starting ability predicts learning rate; practice benefit is conditional on ability.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Charness chess studies found solitary study the strongest practice predictor of tournament rating, yet Ericsson later rejected these studies from the deliberate practice meta-analysis.
numbers: Charness 2005: Study 1 N=239, Study 2 N=169 (Charness 1996 initial N=136).
limits: Criterion shifted over time (teacher or coach required), per the critics.
agent_relevance: Inclusion rules should be fixed before looking at results.

source: Macnamara, Moreau & Hambrick (2022) What makes a champion? Early multidisciplinary practice, not early specialization, predicts world-class performance
finding: World-class athletes had more multisport childhood practice, started later, did less main-sport practice and progressed more slowly than national-class athletes.
numbers: 51 reports, 477 effect sizes, 6,096 athletes including 772 world-class. Nobel laureates showed the same pattern versus national award winners.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. Author order as indexed by Europe PMC is not verified.
agent_relevance: Narrow early practice trades long-term ceiling for fast early gains; compare overfitting to one task.

source: McGaghie et al. (2011) Does simulation-based medical education with deliberate practice yield better results than traditional clinical education?
finding: Applied intervention: simulation training with deliberate practice beat traditional clinical education for specific skills.
numbers: 14 studies from 3,742 identified (1990-2010). Overall effect size 0.71 (95% CI 0.65-0.76).
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. Small study count; skill-specific outcomes; not a test of the elite-performance claim.
agent_relevance: Where goals and feedback are explicit, targeted repetition gives a solid intervention-level effect (about 0.7).

source: Philips et al. (2026) A randomized controlled pilot study comparing ChatGPT to live coaching deliberate practice to teach difficult conversations
finding: Pilot RCT: practice with ChatGPT or with a simulated patient plus live feedback both improved a communication checklist score.
numbers: N=25 anesthesiology trainees (ChatGPT n=13, simulated patient n=12). Both groups improved on a 16-item checklist; abstract gives no between-group effect size.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. Tiny pilot.
agent_relevance: An LLM can play practice partner and feedback source; evidence is small and preliminary.

source: Song (2026) Deliberate practice in the age of AI: AI-assisted practice, self-regulated learning and expert performance in conservatory musicians
finding: Longitudinal observational study: use of AI-assisted practice apps predicted later self-regulated learning, which predicted later instructor-rated performance.
numbers: N=600 recruited, 512 completed 3 waves over 16 weeks. T1 AI practice -> T2 SRL beta=0.47, p<.001; T2 SRL -> T3 performance beta=0.39, p<.001. CFA CFI=.96, RMSEA=.045.
limits: Observational, self-report Likert composites, heterogeneous apps; the author says associations, not causal effects.
agent_relevance: AI tools help by supporting self-regulation, not by being deliberate practice themselves.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: The propensity to practice is itself heritable: about 50% for accumulated music practice.
numbers: Mosing 2014 average heritability about 50% for practice amount; general cognitive ability heritability 50-70% in developed countries.
limits: Review text.
agent_relevance: Practice hours are partly an effect of aptitude, which confounds correlational estimates.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the deliberate practice view defensible?
finding: Duckworth 2011 Spelling Bee found solitary study the best predictor and fully mediating grit; Ericsson's later criteria rejected this study too.
numbers: E&H's education category keeps only this study: r=.31, k=1.
limits: Single study; spelling domain.
